name: Replit
summary: Replit is a Foster City cloud development platform whose AI Agent builds and deploys full apps from prompts for 50M+ users, valued at $9B after a $400M Series D led by Georgian (March 2026). It is the most agentic target in the ICP: its agent writes code, runs it and touches live infrastructure, and it already had a public July 2025 incident where the agent deleted a customer's production database. It runs SOC 2 Type II and has security hiring open, so budget and urgency both exist.
product: Browser-based development and hosting platform. Agent (Agent 4 launched March 2026) builds, runs and deploys apps, slides and videos from prompts, with multiple agents working in parallel; enterprise tier adds Azure Marketplace and Microsoft Fabric data connectors (private preview).

ai_usage.what: AI Agent that builds and deploys apps from prompts, executes code and shell actions, and wires databases and secrets for end users (company_review: customer-facing LLM yes, confidence high).
surfaces: Apps built by users that themselves embed LLMs

customers: Consumers, founders and non-coders (50M+ users per Sacra via tech-insider, March 2026)

funding.last_round: corporate_round (Visa); latest priced round Series D $400M at $9B led by Georgian

headcount.growth_note: Crunchbase range looks stale against ~$525M ARR (Sacra, Apr 2026) and 13 funding rounds; expect materially larger. Several security roles open.

hiring_signals.role: Cloud Security Lead (multi-tenant AI infrastructure, agentic systems preferred)

compliance.soc2: SOC 2 Type II (via Vanta), per replit.com/security
compliance.eu_ai_act_exposure: Indirect: GDPR stated; Replit is a provider of an agent and its users deploy AI apps to EU end users. No EU AI Act statement found.
compliance.notes: ISO 27001 in progress. Shared responsibility model puts app content on the customer, which leaves agent-action and generated-app risk contested. Each customer gets an isolated GCP project; containers use seccomp-bpf, moving to microVMs.

why_now: Replit raised $400M at $9B on 2026-03-11 with Agent 4 (parallel autonomous agents), added Visa as a strategic investor on 2026-05-28, and is posting Cloud Security Lead and AI Agent Security Architect roles to sell into enterprise via Azure; the July 2025 agent database deletion is still being cited (CIO, 2026-10-09), so buyers are asking how agent actions are controlled.
likely_pains: Agents taking destructive actions on production data or infrastructure (the July 2025 database deletion; OWASP LLM06 Excessive Agency)
Prompt injection through repos, packages and web content the agent reads, leading to secret exfiltration or malicious code
Cross-tenant data leakage in multi-tenant AI infrastructure and in apps the agent generates
Abuse of free-tier compute: phishing sites, malware, spam and crypto-mining built through the agent (the same abuse Lovable cites)
Agent misreporting what it did or what is recoverable (documented wrong rollback advice)
Enterprise security reviews demanding auditable agent controls as Replit sells through Azure and Fabric

metrics.hypothesis: Reduced agent-caused incidents and credit refunds, faster enterprise security-review close, lower abuse and compute cost on free tier.

economic_buyer.hypothesis: CTO Luis Chavez, or the head of security once the AI Agent Security Architect is hired; President/Head of AI Michele Catasta is the alternate.

decision_criteria.hypothesis: Latency overhead on agent loops, coverage of tool calls and shell actions, custom natural-language policies per tenant/plan, audit trail, build versus buy against an in-house Security Agent.

decision_process.hypothesis: Engineering-led pilot on a slice of agent traffic, then security and CTO sign-off; likely a short, technical evaluation.

paper_process.hypothesis: Unknown. Expect a vendor security review (they run Vanta) and DPA; White Circle's SOC 2 helps.

identify_pain.hypothesis: The 2025 production-database deletion and a continuing stream of agent-safety scrutiny; company already built dev/prod separation and a Security Agent, so the gap is runtime enforcement on agent actions.

champion.hypothesis: The AI Agent Security Architect once hired, or an agent-platform engineering lead (VP Eng Scott Kennedy's org).

competition.hypothesis: In-house build (strong engineering culture, Security Agent already exists), model-lab guardrails, and Lakera, Prompt Security or Protect AI.

persona_angles.angle: After Agent 4 started running parallel agents against live infrastructure, how are you enforcing per-action policies without adding latency to the loop?
Policies written in plain language that check every agent tool call in real time would let your agent team change rules without retraining anything.
Your open Agent Security Architect role suggests you are designing agent controls now; we can show a runtime layer that blocks or escalates destructive actions and logs which policy fired.
Your shared-responsibility model leaves agent behavior contested; an audit trail of every blocked or allowed agent action gives you evidence after an incident.
Lovable uses us to catch phishing sites and malware requests in agent sessions; do you have the same abuse stream on free-tier builds?

risks: Strong in-house engineering and an existing Security Agent make build-versus-buy the main objection
No head of security or CISO found publicly; economic buyer unclear
Crunchbase headcount looks stale; company may be larger and slower to engage
Latency sensitivity on the agent loop
Competitor to Lovable, White Circle's only named logo (could help or hurt)
HIPAA not claimed by Replit, so compliance leverage is SOC 2 and agent audit trail only
